title: How to organize the feeding station | Nursery
description:
Puts a clean assembled bottle or a full set of pump parts into your hands at 2 a.m.

This is the Feeding Station in the Nursery. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One bin of clean bottles assembled with teats and collars on, a second bin of used parts waiting, a drying rack standing empty, the formula scoop inside the tin with the lid shut, and a stack of burp cloths you can grab without looking.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Line up every bottle, teat, valve, membrane, and pump part on the surface at once.
Straighten: Two bins in obviously different colors, one for clean and ready, one for used and waiting.
Shine: Wash and sterilize on the schedule your kit calls for, then let parts air dry completely before they go into t
Safety: Kettles, bottle warmers, and sterilizers sit at roughly the same height as the changing pad, so a pulled cord
Standardize: Write the formula scoop-to-water numbers you actually use on a card taped above the station, so a grandparent
Sustain: When the kitchen light goes off for the night, the used bin goes down to be washed and the clean bin comes bac

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Clean and ready never shares a bin with used and waiting.
